result.title: Learning Stratified Policies for Inference-Time Objectives
result.summary: Inference-time scaling improves the performance of large language models by sampling multiple responses and evaluating their collective utility. However, many existing approaches obtain these samples by repeatedly sampling from a single policy. In this work, we study if the sample budget at inference time can instead be allocated across a population of policies. We introduce stratified policies, where each of $k$ learned policies contributes one response to a $k$-sample inference-time objective. We realize this policy population using separate LoRA adapters on a shared language model backbone and optimize it for pass@$k$. We theoretically motivate the approach by analyzing the linear setting; a population of LoRAs can achieve zero best-of-$k$ approximation error in settings where every single LoRA has strictly positive prediction error. Empirically, we demonstrate that stratified policies consistently improve pass@$k$ over a single-policy baseline across multiple reasoning tasks. Overall, our results highlight how distributing samples across complementary policies can be a more effective use of sample budget than repeated i.i.d. sampling from a single policy at inference time.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究把推理时采样预算分配给 k 个独立 LoRA 策略组成的「策略群体」，每个策略贡献一条回答以优化 pass@k，并用线性设定分析说明群体可取得单一策略无法达到的 best-of-k 近似误差，在多类推理任务上验证收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「把采样预算分配到互补候选源」的思路可供核查是否能用于 VLM 多候选推理轨迹的生成与验证预算安排；但该工作只在纯文本输出层做多次采样，未涉及视觉状态或 latent 推理表示，向 LVR 的迁移需较多核查。
